target_customer: Home buyers wanting to cut agent commission costs
problem: Buyers paid full agent commissions for work that mostly involved a few tours and paperwork; Open Listings used on-demand agents and rebated half the commission.
business_model: Discount brokerage that refunded about half of buyer agent commission

founders.name: Alex Farrill
founders.background_notes: Later Head of Engineering for Buyer at Opendoor.

competitors.name: Redfin
competitors.what: Salaried agent discount brokerage with listing search

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace software and offer workflows were standard; the hard part was licensing and operating as a brokerage state by state.

defensibility.rationale: Brokerage licenses and agent supply are modest barriers, but the discount model was copyable by Redfin and others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Opendoor acquired Open Listings in September 2018 and folded the brand into Opendoor by early 2019.

market_need_then: Buyers resented commissions of about 3 percent; the founders had bought homes themselves, and early coverage said the startup saved buyers thousands of dollars.

branding.domain_note: openlistings.com, later redirected to a goodbye page on Opendoor's domain.

rebrands.why: Opendoor said a unified brand and app gave customers the best experience.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name with no brand assets found, and the brand was retired within six months of the acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Open Listings raised a roughly 1 million dollar seed in 2015 and a 6.5 million Series A led by Matrix in 2017, expanded to five markets with about 45 employees, and was bought by Opendoor in September 2018 for an undisclosed sum. Opendoor wanted a buy-side brokerage to pair with its iBuying, and retired the brand in early 2019. It succeeded as a strategic acquisition rather than a standalone company.
notes: openlistings.com fetch failed with a DNS error; per Inman and Wikipedia snippets it redirects to an Opendoor goodbye page. Seed amount is reported as roughly 1M in a SoCal Tech snippet and Seedtable agrees at 1M; CB Insights totals 6.62M. Wikipedia lists founding March 2014 while YC says 2015. Redfin as competitor is inferred from a secondary summary of a 2015 article and low confidence. Acquisition price undisclosed. The YC page status Acquired matches the exit.
